_about: H-eye (1 Oct play-test D15h, decision 27; js/clinic/heal/games/eye.js): drops in a front close-up (only the sore eye red, the dropper over it), then the eye test in two versions (test.version: A the split screen, B side by side with the chart on a stand; the lab's ?eyetest=a|b picks either). Chart rows light and tick like card rows; after na the dropper hangs over the eye and pulses. The chart's pictures are Cook's icons for words the child knows (data/clinic/lang.json ids). Sides are said only in the diagnosis (D10). art: the art plan's Y1-Y3, T1, T2, C1, C2 swap in by file name once ready. The older keys below (numbers, chart_nouns, levels) are the first design's notes, kept for Mum's word list; the game's levels are in its code (K).

1._note: Drops (the count; the sore eye shows, so no side row) + three chart calls, rows of 3, 4, 5. Lines come one at a time.

2._note: + the side, in the patient's voice (no eye looks sorer than the other); four calls. Said as one list.

3._note: + the patch on THE OTHER eye (the only reversed side in any mode); five calls with wadho/nindho and a nar row.

camera._about: D2 (1 Oct): the wide shot the zoom starts from, chosen by the angle the close-up needs (front-on or side-on). No side-on sitting pose exists yet: 'side' uses the front pose until the art batch (art list A1).
camera._target: A1 (5 Oct): the match cut. target = where the close-up draws the sore part and size = its radius, in the close-up's 800 x 500 units: the push-in ends with the patient's part (from the art's anchor) at that place and size.

test._about: A = the split screen (the patient close up covering one eye, looking over our shoulder; the chart on the right); B = the patient side-on at the left, a big chart on a stand at the right, turned a quarter towards both (D15h: both prototyped for Zafar)

art._about: art plan pack clinic-heal-v3: used once ready is true ({kind} = the patient's kind); box = x, y, w, h in the close-up's 800x500 units; eye = where the open eye is (the redrop)

eyesSore._note: Y2: the sore eye on the viewer's right (the patient's left): the code mirrors it for the other side
eyesSore._a1: A1 (5 Oct): Y2 at 0.81, its eyes' midpoint (769, 695 in the 1536 x 1024 source) on (400, 250), so the face leaves by the bottom too; eyes = where that puts the patient's right and left eye ([right x, left x, y]: the game's drops and dropper follow). The run framed Y1/Y2 wider than asked (redo list). The blink waits for Y3.

eyesClosed._a1: A1 (5 Oct): Y3 on Y2's canvas: the blink after each drop.

testA._a1: A1 (5 Oct): T1, mirrored in the cut so she looks at the chart (the run's picture looked away); slice-fitted into the left panel; eye = her open eye there.

testB._a1: A1 (5 Oct): T2 meet-fitted into the left of the scene; eye = her eye there.

chartFront._a2: A2 (5 Oct): C1; board = the white board's corners (shares of the picture: top-left, top-right, bottom-right, bottom-left), lines = its six ruled lines as shares of the board's height. The rows of pictures sit on the lines under the eye, the biggest at the top.

chartTurned._a2: A2 (5 Oct): C2, the same chart turned on its easel; board = its four corners, so the rows are laid on it in perspective; lines are C1's.

eyes._a1: A1 (5 Oct): Y1, the clear eyes on Y2's canvas: fades in over the sore eye with each drop.
